newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sees continued strong ties with Japan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sees continued strong ties with Japan.

text.p: The United States said Monday it expected to have continued strong and cooperative relations with Japan following Sunday's Japanese elections.

"We obviously congratulate Prime Minister (Ryutaro) Hashimoto on his own re-election to the Diet," White House press secretary Mike McCurry told reporters during a campaign stop with President Bill Clinton in Parma, Ohio.

"We look forward to working with the new Japanese government when it is formed. We don't pre-suppose the nature of the coalition that might be formed, but the United States has enjoyed excellent working relationships with Prime Minister Hashimoto," he said.
At the State Department, spokesman Nicholas Burns said Washington watched the election with great interest because of the importance of U.S.-Japan ties.
"The United States expects to continue a very strong cooperative relationship that we have enjoyed with Japan over the years," he told a news briefing.
"We look forward to working with the next government and we certainly look forward to working with all the ministers that are appointed in that government."

Burns added: "The U.S.-Japan relationship is the fundamental key to stability in Asia, it's an exceedingly critical relationship. These were important elections and we hope to continue to have a productive, and sustained excellent relationship with Japan in the future."

Hashimoto's Liberal Democratic Party secured 239 seats in Sunday's voting, 12 short of the 251 it needed to govern alone in the 500-seat Lower House. The prime minister met his old allies on Monday to try to convince them to join a new governing coalition after voters denied the LDP a clear mandate.
